_: The last rung of the tone ladder: the knee has landed at 0.5, so this asks two things — how high
the ceiling should stand (`white`) and whether the light the fold takes off the sunlit half should
be paid back with the exposure.
It answers that the white point barely touches the sunlit half — 29 bytes of room at 0.96
against 30 at 1.0 — and what it does move is the top of the picture, where a sun glint on the
water and a lamp's glass live: capped at 0.96 the whole Villa is held under byte 247 and those
go grey-white instead of white. So the shipped curve leaves the ceiling at 1.0 and moves only
the knee and the desaturation. The exposure pays the light back: 0.72 leaves the start view three
points under where the Villa stands today, 0.76 one point off it, and 0.78 a point over.
One warning off these numbers: the same case twice in one run moves the whole-frame luminance by
two or three points, because the water is animated and the film grain is animated too. Nothing
smaller than that is a real difference here.
